Macrons

Consonantal i

Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

life noun

also lifetime, all my life, in my life, way of life, that’s life

classical

Cic. Att. 5.20.6: in vītā meā
Cic. Fam. 9.20.3: haec igitur est nunc vīta nostra

vīta, vītae f.

noun, first declension

life: being alive, a lifetime, a way of living

It covers both senses of English “life”: being alive (in vītā manēre, to stay alive, Cic. Fam. 5.15.3, Lewis & Short) and the life one leads (vīta rūstica, Cic. Rosc. Am. 48, Lewis & Short). Mea vīta is also an endearment (Cic. Fam. 14.4.1).

Examples

  • ego in vītā meā nūllā umquam voluptāte tantā sum adfectus quantā adficior hāc integritāte

    never in my life have I felt such pleasure as I feel at this honesty of mineCic. Att. 5.20.6

  • haec igitur est nunc vīta nostra: māne salūtāmus domī

    so this is our life now: in the morning we receive callers at homeCic. Fam. 9.20.3

  • Ita vīta est hominum quasi cum lūdās tesserīs

    human life is like a game of diceTer. Ad. 739

  • quod hodiē nōn est, crās erit: sīc vīta trūditur

    what isn’t here today will be tomorrow: that’s how life goes onPetr. 45.1

Other words

  • aetās, aetātis f. — lifetime; a time of life

    noun, third declension · also used · classical · Cic. Sen. 70: breve enim tempus aetātis satis longum est ad bene honestēque vīvendum

    The span of a life, or one stage of it, from childhood to old age.

  • vīctus, vīctūs m. — way of living, daily life

    noun, fourth declension · also used · classical · Cic. Off. 1.58: vīta vīctusque commūnis (Lewis & Short, s.v. vīta)

    The means and manner of living, food above all (see diet).

See also live, die, be born, health.
